summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei. Monthly inflation was 1.9% in September, in line with the central bank's survey of economists and up from 1.7% in August, and yearly inflation is 33.4%. Prices are up 23.6% so far in 2026. Reserves were about $48.7 billion on Oct 5 and the central bank has been buying dollars. The IMF's third program review is still open after a Sep 21 to 29 mission. Argentine stocks move on inflation prints, reserves and the IMF, and energy names also ride Vaca Muerta shale output and oil prices. On Oct 22 country risk topped 700 (709), the official dollar hit a nominal record of 1,550 pesos and the Merval fell 1.5% to 97,993.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

summary: Lula won the Oct 25 runoff, and Brazil has sold off three days in a row: the Ibovespa fell 13.88% on Oct 26, 0.51% on Oct 27 and 2.68% to 171,006.10 on Oct 28 on doubts about economic policy (InfoMoney, UOL). The real is holding near R$5.34 per dollar because markets price a Selic hike when the central bank meets Nov 3 to 4, with the Selic at 13.75%. In New York EWZ fell 1.98% to 33.62 on Oct 28 on 2.08 times its 50 day volume, and NU dropped to 11.97 (Massive). Farm credit is already tight: AGCO says Brazil tractor retail sales fell 17% in the first nine months of 2026. The test is whether Lula's team gives a credible spending plan before the rate decision.
for_you: No Brazil buys, swings or new puts until the Nov 3 to 4 rate decision. NU closed at 11.97 on Oct 28, 8.6% below its 13.10 'thesis broken' line, and stays Wait. MELI stays Avoid; EWZ, ITUB and PBR have no verdict. An EWZ Nov 20 $37 put is 9.1% in the money at 33.62; with no verdict, do not roll.

summary: The US and China extended their trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. Chinese stocks are weak: the CSI 300 entered a bear market on Oct 22, 20.2% below its June peak. The yuan is the bright spot: it rose to 6.6620 per dollar on Oct 29, a four year high, helped by central bank guidance and the Fed's hold (Reuters via Economic Times). Q3 GDP grew 4.5% while shoppers stayed weak, and the record trade surplus raises the odds of a new tariff fight before Jan 10.
for_you: China matters to you mostly through US names that sell there and through memory supply. A stronger yuan helps US exporters' China sales a little. No action; Chinese ADRs are not on the buy zone list.

summary: Europe is fighting an energy shock from the Iran war: euro area inflation was 3.2% in August with energy up 14.3%, and the ECB decides Oct 29 with its deposit rate at about 2.50%. The euro fell to a 17 month low against the dollar on Oct 28 as the dollar rose and French fiscal worries lingered (Dow Jones via Morningstar). France's budget revenue vote is Nov 3, after Moody's kept it at Aa3 with a negative outlook on Oct 23. UBS's Q3 profit of $2.69 billion missed the $2.71 billion forecast, and the ECB approved Intesa Sanpaolo's 31.4 billion euro takeover of Monte dei Paschi. ASML is still the European name that matters most for the AI themes.
for_you: A weak euro helps European exporters like ASML and SAP in dollar terms but raises Europe's oil bill. European bank ADRs (SAN, ING) stay a wait until France's Nov 3 vote. The ECB decides Oct 29.

summary: The US-Iran war that began Feb 28, 2026 has kept the Strait of Hormuz mostly shut to commercial traffic. Brent settled up 1.3% at $115.32 on Oct 28 after Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi Arabia and a WSJ report of US plans for action after the Nov 3 midterms (The National). On Oct 29 it fell 1.73% to $113.32 after Vice President Vance reached out to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei and Qatar offered a new peace proposal, which a senior Iranian official rejected (CNBC). Oil now swings on headlines both ways within a day. Most Gulf champions like Aramco are not US listed, so the US trade runs through oil producers, LNG exporters, oil service firms and the KSA ETF.
for_you: This is the biggest outside risk to the dashboard, and it has a date: the days after Nov 3. XOM and CVX report Oct 30; by her volume rule their swings were never confirmed, so take profits or tighten stops today and do not add. Oil service names like BKR are hurt, not helped, by the closed Gulf.

summary: India's central bank raised its repo rate 0.25 point to 5.50% on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023, as oil above $100 pushed inflation up. September consumer inflation was 5.54%, above the RBI's 5.2% forecast. On Oct 29 the Sensex jumped 905.01 points to 74,151.04 and the Nifty 1.05% to 22,936.75 on bank and consumer buying after the Fed's pause (Deccan Herald), and the rupee firmed 3 paise to 95.25 per dollar (Economic Times). Lower oil this week helps India, which imports most of its crude. A 10% US Section 301 tariff still applies to most Indian goods, and the February trade deal has stalled.
for_you: India helps outsourcers (INFY, WIT) through a weak rupee and hurts banks and travel through higher rates. Nothing here is on your lists; low priority.

summary: The peso fell to about 18.4 per dollar on Oct 9, its weakest since November 2025. The trigger was Banxico's Oct 8 minutes, which left the door open to rate cuts from 6.50% and said Mexico need not follow the Fed, so the carry trade that held the peso up is weakening. The USMCA was not renewed in July and moved to annual reviews, so trade rules for cars and factories stay uncertain. A weaker peso cuts the dollar value of Mexican companies' profits but lowers costs for companies that make goods in Mexico and sell in the US.
for_you: A weaker peso and rate cuts help the airport stocks (ASR, PAC) more than consumer names. Nothing here is a setup today. Watch only if you want Mexico exposure.

summary: Korea is a memory chip market, and it swings hardest on AI news. SK hynix's record quarter lifted the KOSPI 6.63% on Oct 28, but on Oct 29 Samsung's record profit of 107.44 trillion won only matched estimates and it put off new shareholder returns until January, so its shares fell 4.13% and the KOSPI 1.24% to 5,937.66 (CNBC, TradingKey). Samsung says HBM is sold out for next year and chip markets stay tight through 2028, and it will raise chip capex 62% (Reuters). The Bank of Korea held at 3.00% on Oct 22 and says more hikes depend on Q3 GDP and inflation. US investors reach Korea mostly through EWY, the SK hynix ADR (SKHY), Korean bank ADRs and Coupang.

summary: Taiwan's story is the AI chip boom. Foreign investors have still been cutting AI exposure on rate and debt fears. On Oct 29 the Taiex fell 667.25 points, or 1.42%, to 46,368.33 and lost its quarterly moving average, as United Microelectronics hit limit down after its earnings call (BigGo Finance). The main local risks remain China-Taiwan tension or US chip tariffs; no new tension was found this week.
